monthly_review.summary: You've shifted toward higher-intensity running this month with fewer but faster and more physiologically demanding sessions, reflected in elevated HR, aerobic TE, and Zone 3–4 time — though total volume dropped significantly.
monthly_review.highlight: Your Zone 3–5 time jumped from 22% last month to 55% this month — indicating a sharp, possibly unplanned shift toward threshold and VO2 max work, despite only one run logged.

goal_tracker.message: You need 36.0 more km across 9 additional sessions (avg 4.0 km/session) to match last month’s volume — ideally distributed as 2 easy runs (Z1–Z2), 1 tempo (Z3), 1 interval (Z4), and 5 mixed-effort runs.

insights.title: Efficiency declined despite faster pace
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency dropped from 13.42 to 12.81 km/hr per bpm — meaning you’re expending more HR per unit speed, likely due to increased vertical oscillation (7.5 → 7.9 cm) and ground contact time (316 → 310 ms not improving proportionally to pace gain).

insights.title: Overrepresentation of Zone 3–5 effort
insights.body: This month’s HR zone distribution shows 55% in Zones 3–5 (26% Z3 + 22% Z4 + 7% Z5), up from 22% last month — suggesting insufficient low-intensity recovery or base-building stimulus.

insights.title: Cadence improved but stride length variability increased
insights.body: Cadence rose from 146 to 154 spm, yet stride length varied widely across recent runs (67.6–82.0 cm), especially on the 2.1 km run (81.96 cm at 142 bpm) — hinting at pace/effort mismatch and compromised form under fatigue or intensity.

insights.title: Aerobic TE surged without volume support
insights.body: Avg aerobic TE jumped to 3.5 — a strong stimulus — but occurred in just one 10 km run (vs. ten runs last month averaging 2.7), implying high acute load without chronic load foundation; VO2 max remains stable at 37.0, confirming no adaptation yet.

recommendations.action: Do your next run as a 5 km Zone 2 effort (HR ≤135 bpm) with cadence consciously held at 148–152 spm
recommendations.reason: To rebuild aerobic efficiency and lower HR-per-pace — last month’s Z2-dominant runs (79% Z1+Z2) correlated with higher efficiency (13.42) and lower avg HR (136 bpm).

recommendations.action: Add a 20-min post-run mobility routine focusing on hip flexors and calves after every run this week
recommendations.reason: Ground contact time remains elevated (308–320 ms) and vertical oscillation increased (7.5→8.3 cm), suggesting stiffness or reduced elasticity — especially evident on the short, fast 2.1 km run (8.3 cm VO, 320 ms GCT).

recommendations.action: Repeat your May 22 run (3.5 km @ 9:05 min/km, HR 136 bpm, cadence 150 spm) as a benchmark run this week
recommendations.reason: It represents your most balanced recent effort — moderate pace, low HR drift, stable cadence, and 2.4 aerobic TE — ideal for assessing consistency before ramping intensity.

weekly_focus.description: Re-establish rhythm and efficiency by prioritizing controlled Zone 2 efforts, cadence awareness, and repeatable pacing — countering this month’s outlier intensity spike with reproducible, sustainable stimulus.
suggested_sessions: 5 km Zone 2 tempo (HR ≤135 bpm, cadence 148–152 spm)
3.5 km repeat of May 22 run (9:05 min/km, HR ~136 bpm)
4 km progressive run: start Z2 (132 bpm), finish last km at Z3 (145 bpm)
